skill.name: documentation
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to write clear, structured Markdown documents such as plans, proposals, guides, specs, and READMEs.
skill.summary: Create readable Markdown documents with clear structure, practical tone, and optional Mermaid diagrams.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown prose and inline code formatting in SKILL.md. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, unauthorized command execution, or hidden malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: **Never dump long-form content to the terminal.** Always write to a `.md` file and tell the user whe

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 uses Markdown inline code around the .md file extension, not Ruby or shell execution. The prose only tells the assistant to write long-form documents to Markdown files.
Line 26 uses Markdown inline code around the word mermaid. It references another documentation skill for diagrams and does not invoke a command or pass user input to a shell.
Line 22 describes text formatting to improve document readability. It does not request host inspection, environment enumeration, or any reconnaissance activity.

content.value_statement: Teams often need readable documents that are structured for fast review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce clear Markdown files.
actual_capabilities: Directs assistants to write long-form content to Markdown files.
Promotes headings, bullets, tables, code blocks, and short paragraphs.
Recommends Mermaid diagrams when architecture or process relationships need visuals.
Adapts tone for technical docs, proposals, brainstorms, and plans.
Guides restrained emoji use for navigation and callouts.
limitations: Does not include templates for specific document types.
Does not validate Markdown links, diagrams, or rendered output.
Does not create diagrams itself; it recommends Mermaid when useful.
Does not enforce brand voice or detailed editorial style guides.

use_cases.title: Write Project Plans
use_cases.description: Create actionable plans with clear sections, concise steps, and practical next actions.

use_cases.title: Improve READMEs
use_cases.description: Turn scattered setup notes into readable Markdown that developers can scan quickly.

use_cases.title: Capture Brainstorms
use_cases.description: Organize rough ideas into structured notes without losing exploratory context.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Markdown document for this topic. Use clear headings, short paragraphs, and a concise summary.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a proposal for this initiative. Keep the tone persuasive, honest, and easy to review.

prompt_templates.title: Document a System
prompt_templates.prompt: Write system documentation for this architecture. Include sections for purpose, components, flows, risks, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Documentation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a documentation plan for this project. Define the needed files, audience, structure, diagrams, and review steps.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding notes for a new service.
output_examples.output: A Markdown onboarding guide with overview, setup steps, common tasks, troubleshooting notes, and next actions.

output_examples.input: Turn meeting notes into a project plan.
output_examples.output: A structured plan with goals, decisions, tasks, owners, risks, and follow-up questions.
A technical document with component descriptions, request flow, operational notes, and suggested Mermaid diagrams.

best_practices: Give the intended audience and document purpose before generation.
Ask for diagrams when relationships or flows need visual support.
Review the generated Markdown for factual accuracy before sharing.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a source of verified technical facts.
Do not request long documents without scope or audience context.
Do not rely on it to enforce private style guides automatically.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create Markdown documents such as plans, proposals, notes, guides, specs, and READMEs.

faq.question: Does it write files automatically?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to place long-form content in Markdown files when the host tool supports file writing.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: It does not generate diagrams directly, but it recommends Mermaid diagrams when visual structure would help.

faq.question: Is it only for technical documentation?
faq.answer: No. It also supports proposals, brainstorms, plans, notes, and other structured written documents.

faq.question: Does it replace editing and review?
faq.answer: No. Users should still review facts, tone, links, and any domain-specific requirements.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
